lines.trans: Well, how do you like the new head chef?
She seems a bit boring to me.
On the other hand she is calm and polite.
That is true, she never yells.
With her the kitchen is quiet and pleasant.
Slackers! Scraps! What are you doing?
I returned to restore complete order!
Chef, we were just cleaning the fish.
We are very glad to see you!
Stop chatting and take your knives!
Who permitted you to stand idle?
We will chop everything right now, chef.
Get to work quickly, lively!

meanings.note: Privative prefix 'без-' ('without, -less') (stem 'дельник'). Derived noun with agent/object suffix '-ник'/'-щик'/'-чик'. Common masculine noun meaning 'idler, slacker' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Slackers! Scraps! What are you doing?

examples.text: Да уж, играют как настоящие бездельники!
examples.trans: Indeed, they play like real slackers!

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to chatter, chat, talk idly', paired with 'поболтать'.

examples.text: Не словом, а делом! Все болтают, а я работаю.
examples.trans: Not in word, but in deed! Everyone chatters, while I work.

meanings.note: 'брать' alone often means this, in talk about officials

examples.trans: We have to take all the money.

meanings.note: the comparative 'быстрее', often as an order
the comparative 'быстрее', often as an order

examples.text: Виталик, почему мы так медленно едем? Быстрее!
examples.trans: Vitalik, why are we going so slowly? Faster!

meanings.note: Qualitative adjective formed with the productive suffix '-тельный'/'-ливый'. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('polite, courteous').

examples.trans: On the other hand she is calm and polite.

examples.text: Я улыбнусь и скажу самые вежливые слова.
examples.trans: I will smile and say the most polite words.

examples.text: Спасибо, я стараюсь быть очень вежливым.
examples.trans: Thank you, I try to be very polite.

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to come back, to return', paired with 'возвращаться'.

examples.text: Так, не шумим. Я скоро вернусь.
examples.trans: Right, no noise. I'll be back soon.
I can see the toy car.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: ends a conversation or an order: 'Всё, свободен' = that's all, you can go
at the start of a sentence

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people

meanings.en: other forms: вас (gen/acc), вам (dat), вами (instr), вас (prep)

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to do, to make', paired with 'сделать'.

examples.trans: Hi, Arkady Borisovich. What are you doing?

meanings.note: много дел = a lot to do

examples.trans: I have a lot to do.

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

examples.text: Лёва! Ты ещё здесь? Живо в архив!
examples.trans: Lyova! Are you still here? Off to the archive, now!

зато.gloss: but on the other hand, to make up for it

meanings.en: but on the other hand, at least

examples.text: Четыре по алгебре, зато по физкультуре пятёрка.
examples.trans: A four in algebra, but a five in gym.
The flat is small, but at least it's in the centre.

examples.text: Ничего страшного. Сейчас зато аппетит нагуляем.
examples.trans: No big deal. At least we'll walk up an appetite now.

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: мне кажется = I think, it seems to me

examples.trans: I think I've seen you somewhere.

meanings.note: как вы знаете = as you know

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

examples.text: Не надо кричать. Хорошо, я буду сегодня.
examples.trans: There's no need to shout. All right, I'll be there tonight.
Arkady Borisovich, who are your rivals?
Three rooms and a big kitchen.
And the kitchen is over there.

meanings.note: нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place

meanings.en: other forms: нас (gen/acc), нам (dat), нами (instr), нас (prep)

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!
The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.
I will establish iron order here.

examples.text: Дежурный офицер навёл идеальный порядок в части.
examples.trans: The duty officer established ideal order in the unit.

examples.text: Да, я наведу здесь железный порядок.
examples.trans: Yes, I will establish iron order here.

meanings.note: to cut into portions or pieces

examples.text: Вот теперь кусочки нарезаны красиво и аккуратно.
examples.trans: Now the pieces are cut beautifully and neatly.

examples.text: Сначала мелко нарежь лук и морковь.
examples.trans: First chop the onion and carrot finely.
I will cut the vegetables into even pieces.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'стоящий'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('real, genuine').

examples.text: Ваня, да пойми ты наконец! Это настоящий успех.
examples.trans: Vanya, understand at last! This is real success.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'много'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: I need to do a bit of work.

examples.text: Мы даём вам ещё немного времени.
examples.trans: We are giving you a little more time.

meanings.note: used with не before the verb, or alone

examples.text: Я никогда не был на море.
examples.trans: I've never been to the sea.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('new').

examples.text: Ну что, довольна? Теперь новую работу искать.
examples.trans: Well, happy now? Now I have to look for a new job.

meanings.note: end-stressed in all oblique forms: ножа, ножом

examples.trans: Cutting a living person with a knife!
There is a sharp knife on the table.

examples.text: Нина, ну как ты могла? Живого человека ножом резать!
examples.trans: Nina, how could you? Cutting a living person with a knife!

meanings.note: hesitation, at the start of a sentence

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common masculine noun meaning 'scrap, remnant, core' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Slackers! Scraps! What are you doing?

examples.text: Паша, я больше не хочу о ней слышать. Понял?
examples.trans: Pasha, I don't want to hear about her again. Understood?
I love our town very much.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

examples.text: На столе стоял полный стакан воды.
examples.trans: A full glass of water stood on the table.

examples.text: Ну что я тебе скажу, Аркаша? Это полный кошмар!
examples.trans: Well, what can I tell you, Arkasha? This is a total nightmare!

meanings.note: по порядку = in order; всё в порядке = everything is fine

examples.trans: Now let's go through everything in order.

examples.text: Теперь давай всё по порядку. Скажи мне, сколько ты им должна?
examples.trans: Now let's go through everything in order. Tell me, how much do you owe them?

meanings.note: as a side word: Правда, всё нормально = Honestly, everything's fine
as a side word: Правда, всё нормально = Honestly, everything's fine

examples.text: Правда, Нин, всё нормально. Скажи что-нибудь, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: Honestly, Nina, everything's fine. Say something, please.

meanings.en: to stop, put an end to

examples.trans: Stop it! We will have the flat.

examples.text: Да ну что вы, прекратите! Это жизнь.
examples.trans: Oh, come on, stop it! That's life.

meanings.note: очень приятно = pleased to meet you

examples.text: Очень приятно. А в чём дело?
examples.trans: Pleased to meet you. So what's the matter?

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

meanings.note: short form only: рад, рада, радо, рады; no long-form cases

examples.trans: I'm very glad to see you.

examples.text: Ну что ты? Я очень рад тебя видеть.
examples.trans: Oh, come on! I'm very glad to see you.

meanings.note: polite formula, at a door or before asking something

examples.trans: May we come in? Good day, sir.
A big platter of fish and crabs.

examples.text: На ужин мы приготовили свежую рыбу.
examples.trans: For dinner we cooked fresh fish.

examples.text: У нас есть большая тарелка рыбы и крабов.
examples.trans: We have a big platter of fish and crabs.

meanings.note: + instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

examples.text: Этот материал слишком старый и скучный.
examples.trans: This material is far too old and boring.
She seems a bit boring to me.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'нова').

examples.text: Нормально? Она через неделю снова потечёт!
examples.trans: Fine? It'll be leaking again in a week!

examples.text: Это ваша самоуверенность промелькнула. Спокойной ночи!
examples.trans: That was your overconfidence flashing by. Good night!

meanings.note: the infinitive 'Стоять!' as a police order
the infinitive 'Стоять!' as a police order

examples.text: То есть просто стоять и смотреть?
examples.trans: So we just stand and watch?

meanings.en: other forms: тебя (gen/acc), тебе (dat), тобой (instr), тебе (prep)

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

examples.text: Там мне дают только чистить овощи.
examples.trans: There they only give me vegetables to peel.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

examples.trans: The chef is in the kitchen.

examples.text: Шеф-повар лично руководит работой на кухне.
examples.trans: The head chef personally oversees the work in the kitchen.
The head chef manages the entire kitchen.

examples.text: Они привели нового шеф-повара прямо из Индии.
examples.trans: They brought a new chef straight from India.

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine

meanings.en: other forms: этого, этому, это, этим, этом

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)
